nodes.name: RhPd-H solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis, 8 mg of Pd(acac)₂, 8 mg of Rh(acac)₃ and 120 mg of PVP were added into a mixed solution containing 3 mL of benzyl alcohol and 3 mL of acetaldehyde. The solution was stirred vigorously for 1 h to form a homogeneous solution and then transferred into a 10 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. Then, the vessel was sealed and heated from room temperature to 180°C in 30 min and kept at this temperature for another 8 h before it was naturally cooled to room temperature. The resulting products were collected by centrifugation (12000 rpm, 10 min) and washed with cyclohexane and ethanol (1:1) three times.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows RhPd-H NPs as irregular polyhedra with average size of 15.6 ± 2.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images, the dominant products of the RhPd-H NPs are irregular polyhedra with an average size of 15.6 ± 2.5 nm (Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution HAADF-STEM shows lattice spacing of 0.231 nm on (111) facets of RhPd-H NPs, 3.6% larger than RhPd NPs (0.223 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing on the (111) facets of the RhPd-H NPs is 0.231 nm, which is ∼3.6% larger than that of the RhPd NPs (0.223 nm) (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows Rh and Pd distributed throughout the entire RhPd-H NP, indicating alloying.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping show that both the Rh and Pd elements are distributed throughout the entire particle, indicating alloying (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows smaller radius (lattice expansion) for RhPd-H NPs compared to RhPd NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We found that the radius in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the RhPd-H NPs is smaller than that of the RhPd NPs, suggesting that the lattice is expanded in the RhPd-H NPs (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS plasmon resonance peaks at ~5.5 eV across RhPd-H NPs (surface and interior), much lower than ~8 eV for RhPd NPs, indicating hydrogen modification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Peaks from three positions on the RhPd-H NPs are located at approximately 5.5 eV (Figure 1g), which is much lower than those on the RhPd NPs (∼8 eV) (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD peaks of RhPd-H NPs shift to lower angle vs RhPd NPs indicating lattice expansion; H:(Rh+Pd) ratio of 0.4 by Vegard's law.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic XRD peaks of the RhPd-H NPs shift to lower angle compared with those of the RhPd NPs, indicating expansion of the lattice and alloyed hydride structures... The XRD patterns also indicate that the RhPd-H NPs have a H: (Rh + Pd) ratio of 0.4 based on Vegard's law.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows new peaks at 882, 1040, 1090, and 1128 cm⁻¹ in RhPd-H NPs matching simulated H-modified RhPd, excluding C modification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Four new FTIR peaks located at 882, 1040, 1090, and 1128 cm⁻¹ were observed in the FTIR spectra of RhPd-H NPs compared with that of RhPd NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS valence band spectra show narrower bandwidth for RhPd-H NPs than RhPd NPs; Pd 3d and Rh 3d peaks shift +0.67 eV and +0.30 eV respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The RhPd-H NPs show a narrower bandwidth than the RhPd NPs (Figure 2b)... The Pd and Rh 3d peaks of the RhPd-H NPs shift to higher binding energies by 0.67 and 0.30 eV compared with those of the RhPd NPs, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd K-edge EXAFS shows Pd-Pd/Rh bond length 2.800 Å (vs 2.745 Å) and coordination number 7.3 (vs 7.8) for RhPd-H NPs; similar trends at Rh K-edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transforms (FT) of the EXAFS spectra of the Pd K-edge... reveal that the Pd-Pd/Rh bond length of the RhPd-H NPs is 2.800 Å which is longer than that of the RhPd NPs (2.745 Å). Meanwhile, the coordination number of the Pd atoms in the RhPd-H NPs is 7.3, which is smaller than that in the RhPd NPs (7.8).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDX mapping confirm alloying with each element (Pd, Rh, Ru) distributed throughout RuPd-H NPs and RuRhPd-H NPs; Ru shell observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HADDF-STEM and EDX elemental mapping images show that each element (Pd, Rh, and Ru) is distributed throughout the entire particle, indicating alloying (Figure 5a-h).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of RuPd-H NPs and RuRhPd-H NPs show alloyed hydride nanostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns (Figure 5i), high-resolution HAADF-STEM images (Figure S31), valence band structures (Figures S32 and S33), and FTIR spectra (Figure S34) clearly show the alloyed hydride nanostructures of RuPd-H NPs and RuRhPd-H NPs.
